079195f49b240886327a8d1c7f7fdfadca92ca01: Why altitude matters: on average, the temperature drops by about 0.6 °C every 100 metres. The higher a ski area goes, the better its chances of keeping snow for longer, especially at the start and end of the season. The highest point, however, is not the altitude of the villages: a ski area can peak at 3,000 m while its villages sit at 1,800 m, and the orientation of the runs also affects snow quality.

07d7b5345093f9e311b6deb2e6b9aa1a71b760c9: Small-scale resort, Bolquère-Pyrénées 2000 focuses on the quality of its welcome and its closeness rather than on impressive figures. Its 42 km of runs are ideal for a stay of 3 to 4 days, especially for families or skiers who don't need to constantly change their playground. Bolquère-Pyrénées 2000's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, a well-organised childcare service, well-maintained green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It's one of the most reassuring resorts in the Pyrenees for laying the foundations of skiing with children. Bolquère-Pyrénées 2000's altitude (1800 m at the bottom, 2200 m at the top) allows it to maintain decent snow reliability in mid-winter. January and February are the most dependable; in December and March, it's worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. The 25€ day lift pass remains reasonable for the quality of the ski area on offer. Counting accommodation, skiing and meals, Bolquère-Pyrénées 2000 suits those who want to spend a lovely week without the final bill knocking them off their chair. In short: Bolquère-Pyrénées 2000 doesn't rival the giants of skiing, and doesn't pretend to. It's an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
